DOUBLE_DECODE_BYPASS.description: Compares live server behavior on a singly-encoded vs. double-encoded path-traversal-style payload. A discrepancy (double-encoded request gets further than the single-encoded one) is evidence the input is decoded/canonicalized more than once before validation.

CRLF_HEADER_REFLECTION.description: Injects an encoded CRLF sequence plus a marker header name/value into common redirect/reflection query parameters and checks whether the marker comes back as a literal response header. This is a reflection-based approximation of V4.2.4 (app-level header injection), not a protocol-level HTTP/2/3 frame-validation test.

OPEN_REDIRECT_LIVE.description: Confirms, against the live target, whether common redirect/callback query parameters — or a forged Host header — drive an unvalidated external redirect. Live-exploitability check for the same control the static UNVALIDATED_REDIRECT taint rule flags at the source level.

REQUEST_SMUGGLING.description: Sends a request with an ambiguous Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding combination immediately followed by a distinctly-marked second request on the same connection, then checks whether the marker leaks into the first response — evidence the front-end/back-end chain disagrees on request framing. Best-effort indicator, not a full exploit chain. Gated behind active_mode: a real desync can affect other users' traffic on shared infrastructure, unlike this engine's other checks.

WEBSOCKET_TOKEN_UNAUTH_ISSUANCE.description: Requests a discovered WebSocket/realtime token-issuance endpoint (URL shape: /ws/token, /websocket-ticket, /realtime/auth, ...) once through the scan's authenticated session and once with no credentials at all. If the unauthenticated request also gets back a token/ticket, the endpoint doesn't actually require a prior authenticated session. Only runs when the scan has an authenticated session configured and the path matches a token-issuance shape; otherwise there's nothing to compare against.

WEBSOCKET_TOKEN_DERIVED_FROM_SESSION.description: Requests a discovered WebSocket/realtime token-issuance endpoint through the scan's authenticated session and compares the returned token verbatim against every HTTP session cookie/auth-header value that same session is using. An exact match means the WebSocket token is just the HTTP session token relabeled, not a dedicated value — a FAIL is decisive, but a clean result only proves no *literal* reuse (a cryptographically derived-but-different value isn't detectable this way), so it never passes the control on its own.

CSRF_TOKEN_NOT_VALIDATED.description: Fetches the target, finds the first state-changing (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) form containing a CSRF-token-shaped hidden field, then resubmits the form with that field dropped. A non-4xx response means the server accepted a state-changing request without validating the anti-CSRF token. Gated behind active_mode: a genuinely unprotected form really does perform the action, unlike this engine's read-only checks.

UNAUTHENTICATED_ACCESS_ALLOWED.description: Requests the target once through the scan's authenticated session, then again with no credentials at all. If the anonymous request also returns 2xx where the authenticated one did, the endpoint doesn't appear to actually require authentication — forced-browsing / missing function-level access control. Only runs when the scan has an authenticated session configured; otherwise there's nothing to compare against.

REFLECTED_XSS_LIVE.description: Replays each query parameter the URL already carries (e.g. crawler-discovered /search?q=...) with a unique inert marker tag, then checks whether it comes back unescaped. Live-exploitability check for the same control the static XSS taint rule flags at the source level. Only tests params the URL already has — unlike OPEN_REDIRECT_LIVE/CRLF_HEADER_REFLECTION, reflected XSS has no small fixed universe of semantically-meaningful param names to guess blindly.

SQL_INJECTION_LIVE.description: For each query parameter the URL already carries, appends an always-true (' OR '1'='1) and an always-false (' OR '1'='2) SQL boolean to the existing value and compares the two responses — a real unparameterized query returns visibly different results for the two, or leaks a DB driver error message outright. Live-exploitability check for the same control the static SQL_INJECTION taint rule flags at the source level. Gated behind active_mode: on a write-context param these payloads reach a real query, same risk class as CSRF_TOKEN_NOT_VALIDATED.

COMMAND_INJECTION_LIVE.description: For each query parameter, tries a shell-delimited sleep payload (;, |, backtick, $()) via oracles.timing_oracle — no in-band heuristic exists for blind command injection, so a measurable delay is the first-pass signal (FAIL). Escalates to an out-of-band curl callback using the winning delimiter; a collaborator hit is the reproduced-impact proof (CONFIRMED). Live-exploitability check for the static COMMAND_INJECTION taint rule. Gated behind active_mode: these payloads can execute real commands server-side.

SSTI_LIVE.description: Injects a Jinja/EL/ERB polyglot arithmetic expression computing a random large product; the product appearing in the response (and not in an unmodified baseline) is evidence the template engine evaluates injected syntax (FAIL). Escalates to known Jinja2/Twig/Freemarker RCE gadgets that call back the out-of-band collaborator; a hit is CONFIRMED. Live-exploitability check for the static CODE_INJECTION taint rule (server-side template injection). Gated behind active_mode: the RCE gadgets execute real code server-side.

XXE_LIVE.description: POSTs an external-entity XML document (Content-Type: application/xml) whose DOCTYPE points the entity at the scan's out-of-band collaborator. A callback proves the target's XML parser resolves external entities (CONFIRMED) — there's no in-band signal for a blind XXE, so this check is collaborator-only (NOT_TESTED without one). Live-exploitability check for the static XXE_UNSAFE_XML_PARSER taint rule. Gated behind active_mode: posting arbitrary XML bodies to arbitrary endpoints is a real side-effecting request.

NOSQL_INJECTION_LIVE.description: For each query parameter, replaces it with a bracket-notation MongoDB operator payload (param[$ne]=, param[$gt]=) — the query-string shape several frameworks (e.g. Express+qs) parse into a nested filter object — and compares the response against a definite-non-match control value via oracles.response_diff_oracle. A visible difference is evidence the param reaches an unsanitized NoSQL query filter (boolean-blind, stays FAIL — no further exploitation step). Live-exploitability check for the static NOSQL_INJECTION taint rule. Gated behind active_mode: same write-context-param risk class as SQL_INJECTION_LIVE.

CORS_MISCONFIG_LIVE.description: Sends a single read-only request with an attacker-controlled Origin header and inspects Access-Control-Allow-Origin/-Credentials in the response. Reflecting the probe origin back (optionally combined with Allow-Credentials: true) means any origin can make credentialed cross-site requests and read the response. Cheap and read-only — not gated behind active_mode, same class as OPEN_REDIRECT_LIVE/REFLECTED_XSS_LIVE. Live-exploitability check for the static CORS_MISCONFIGURATION rule.
